<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Intro to logistic regression</h1>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>


In this practical you will:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Fit a model to predict the probability of weak grip (yes or no) from age on the KLOSA data.</li>
  <li>Read the age coefficient and interpret its sign.</li>
  <li>Use the fitted coefficients to predict weak grip for some example ages.</li>
  <li>Repeat the workflow on a second dataset with a negative coefficient.</li>
</ul>

After answering the questions, your completion code will be revealed.

<p>This is the sequence logistic regression follows:</p>

<div class="svg-panel">
<svg viewBox="0 0 860 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Diagram showing the sequence of logistic regression">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arr" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="7" refY="4.5" orient="auto">
      <path d="M0,0 L9,4.5 L0,9 z" fill="#5d7475"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  <rect x="10" y="55" width="170" height="80" rx="10" fill="#e3f4f4" stroke="#00565e" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="95" y="88" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#00565e">Predictor</text>
  <text x="95" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#173234">age, e.g. 70</text>
  <line x1="180" y1="95" x2="230" y2="95" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="235" y="55" width="200" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#00565e" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="335" y="83" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#00565e">Linear score</text>
  <text x="335" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-family="Consolas, monospace" fill="#173234">b0 + b1 &#215; age</text>
  <line x1="435" y1="95" x2="485" y2="95" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="490" y="40" width="185" height="110" rx="10" fill="#fffaf0" stroke="#f5c542" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <text x="582" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#8a6d00">Logistic function</text>
  <text x="582" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-family="Consolas, monospace" fill="#173234">1 / (1 + e&#8315;&#7611;)</text>
  <path d="M 508 142 C 570 142, 595 105, 657 105" fill="none" stroke="#b83b5e" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <line x1="675" y1="95" x2="720" y2="95" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arr)"/>
  <rect x="725" y="55" width="125" height="80" rx="10" fill="#e8f8ef" stroke="#287a4d" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="787" y="88" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#287a4d">Probability</text>
  <text x="787" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#173234">always 0 to 1</text>
</svg>
<p class="svg-caption">First the model calculates a linear score from the predictor and the coefficients. Then the logistic function converts that score into a probability between 0 and 1.</p>
</div>

</section>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 1. Weak grip in the KLOSA data</h2>

We use the same data as the video: 4,184 men aged 45 and above from the Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLOSA).

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Predictor:</strong> <code>age</code> (years)</li>
  <li><strong>Outcome:</strong> <code>weak_grip</code>, which is <code>1</code> when grip strength is 27 kg or less and <code>0</code> otherwise</li>
</ul>

Run the cell to load the data and preview the first few rows.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: read the data</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

klosa <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/the-graph-courses/rsr_resources/refs/heads/main/data/28_klosa_men_grip.csv")

klosa %>%
  select(age, grip, weak_grip) %>%
  head()
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>Our outcome <code>weak_grip</code> only takes the values <code>1</code> and <code>0</code>. What kind of outcome is this, and which function fits the right model for it?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">A <strong>continuous</strong> outcome measured on a numeric scale, best modeled with `lm()`.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">A <strong>binary</strong> outcome with two values (0 and 1), best modeled with `glm(family = binomial)`.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Yes or no outcomes are binary, and logistic regression, fit with glm(family = binomial), models the probability of the 1." data-incorrect="Not quite. The outcome only has two possible values, so it is binary, and we model its probability with glm(family = binomial)."></div>
</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: plot weak grip by age group</h3>

We divide age into 5-year bands. For each band, we calculate the proportion of men with weak grip. The points show these observed proportions, and the line connects them. We have not fitted a model yet.

```{webr-r}
# Calculate the proportion with weak grip in each 5-year age band.
band_props <- klosa %>%
  group_by(age_band = cut_width(age, 5, boundary = 45)) %>%
  summarize(age = mean(age), proportion = mean(weak_grip))

# Plot the observed proportions.
ggplot(band_props, aes(x = age, y = proportion)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkcyan") +
  geom_point(color = "indianred", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Proportion with weak grip")
```

</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Fitting the model</h2>

The observed proportions suggest that a curved line may fit the data well. We will now fit a logistic regression model.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: fit the logistic regression, fill in the blank</h3>

Fill in the outcome (`weak_grip`), predictor (`age`), and family (`binomial`).

```{webr-r}
grip_model <- glm(____ ~ ____, family = ____, data = klosa)
summary(grip_model)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
grip_model <- glm(weak_grip ~ age, family = binomial, data = klosa)
summary(grip_model)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept) -8.8243     0.3193   -27.64   <2e-16 ***
age          0.1168     0.0048    24.57   <2e-16 ***
```

</details>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: add the fitted logistic curve</h3>

Now use the fitted model to get predicted probabilities across a range of ages. Then draw the curve with `geom_line()`. The points are still the observed proportions from the age bands.

```{webr-r}
# Predicted probabilities from grip_model.
age_line <- data.frame(age = seq(min(klosa$age), max(klosa$age), by = 1))
age_line$prob <- predict(grip_model, newdata = age_line, type = "response")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = age_line, aes(x = age, y = prob), color = "gold") +
  geom_point(data = band_props, aes(x = age, y = proportion),
             color = "indianred", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Probability of weak grip")
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>In the summary output, what is the coefficient (the Estimate) for <code>age</code>?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a"><code>-8.8243</code>, in the <strong>(Intercept)</strong> row of the <strong>Estimate</strong> column.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b"><code>0.1168</code>, in the <strong>age</strong> row of the <strong>Estimate</strong> column.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Each predictor gets its own row, and its coefficient is in the Estimate column. -8.8243 is the intercept." data-incorrect="Not quite. Look at the row labeled age and read the Estimate column: 0.1168. The -8.8243 is the intercept."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 3</div>
  <p>The age coefficient <code>0.1168</code> is positive. From its sign alone, what do we learn?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="a">As age increases, the <strong>predicted probability</strong> of weak grip goes <strong>up</strong>.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b">Each extra year of age adds <strong>0.1168</strong> to the <strong>probability</strong> of weak grip.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. A positive coefficient means the probability increases as the predictor increases, so higher age means higher probability. The probability does not rise by a fixed 0.1168 per year." data-incorrect="Not quite. A positive coefficient means the probability increases as the predictor increases. The probability does not rise by a fixed amount each year."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 4</div>
  <p>So the probability does not go up by 0.1168 per year. What does go up by exactly 0.1168 for each extra year of age?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="a">The <strong>probability</strong> of weak grip, measured on the <strong>percentage scale</strong> (0 to 100).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p3" value="b">The <strong>log odds</strong> of weak grip.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Each extra year adds a fixed 0.1168 to the log odds. You do not need to know log odds yet. For now, remember that the sign tells you the direction of the probability change." data-incorrect="Not quite. The quantity that changes by a fixed 0.1168 per year is the log odds. The probability changes by different amounts depending on age."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 2. Predicting a probability by hand</h2>

The two estimates from the summary are the $b_0$ and $b_1$ of the logistic equation. To predict a probability for a specific person, put their age into the equation:

<div class="formula-panel">
$$
\widehat{p}(\text{weak grip}) \;=\; \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(b_0 + b_1 \times \text{age})}}
\;=\; \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(-8.8243 \;+\; 0.1168 \times \text{age})}}
$$
</div>

We can calculate this using a calculator or using R. (Note that in R, `exp(x)` computes $e^{x}$.)

In R, `exp(x)` computes $e^{x}$, so the whole right-hand side is one line of code. Here we predict the probability of weak grip for a 70-year-old man.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: predict a probability by hand</h3>

Fill in the intercept (`-8.8243`) and the age coefficient (`0.1168`).

```{webr-r}
# Probability of weak grip for a 70-year-old
1 / (1 + exp(-(____ + ____ * 70)))
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
1 / (1 + exp(-(-8.8243 + 0.1168 * 70)))
```

This returns about `0.343`. According to our model, a 70-year-old man has roughly a 34% chance of having a weak grip.

</details>

<section class="panel">

<h2>The same prediction with predict()</h2>

R can also calculate the predicted probabilities for us. We create a small data frame of new people, then call `predict()` on the model. Use `type = "response"` to get probabilities.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: predict for several ages</h3>

Fill in the model name (`grip_model`) and the type argument (`"response"`).

```{webr-r}
new_people <- data.frame(age = c(50, 60, 70, 80))
# Here, fill in the model name (grip_model) and the type argument ("response").
predict(____, newdata = new_people, type = ____)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
new_people <- data.frame(age = c(50, 60, 70, 80))
predict(grip_model, newdata = new_people, type = "response")
```

You should see (rounded):

```
     1      2      3      4
0.0482 0.1401 0.3439 0.6277
```

The third value, 0.3439, matches the hand calculation for the 70-year-old (up to rounding, since we typed in rounded coefficients).

</details>

<div class="callout warning">
<p>If you leave out <code>type = "response"</code>, <code>predict()</code> returns the linear score $b_0 + b_1 \times \text{age}$ instead, on the log odds scale.</p>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 5</div>
  <p>From the output of `predict()`, what is the predicted probability of weak grip for an 80-year-old?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="a">About <strong>0.63</strong>.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b">About <strong>0.52</strong>.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The predicted probability of weak grip for an 80-year-old is about 0.63." data-incorrect="Not quite. The predicted probability of weak grip for an 80-year-old is about 0.63."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 3. A second dataset</h2>

In the KLOSA model the coefficient was positive, so the probability increased with age. Let us now examine a second dataset.

The `birthwt` dataset (from the `MASS` package, built into R) records 189 births at a hospital in Springfield, Massachusetts.

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Predictor:</strong> <code>lwt</code>, the mother's weight in pounds at her last menstrual period</li>
  <li><strong>Outcome:</strong> <code>low</code>, which is <code>1</code> if the baby was born with low birth weight (under 2.5 kg) and <code>0</code> otherwise</li>
</ul>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: plot low birth weight against mother's weight</h3>

We divide the mothers' weights into 20-pound bands. For each band, we calculate the proportion of babies with low birth weight. The points show these observed proportions, and the line connects them. We have not fitted a model yet.

```{webr-r}
library(MASS)

bw_props <- birthwt %>%
  group_by(weight_band = cut_width(lwt, 20, boundary = 80)) %>%
  summarize(weight = mean(lwt), proportion = mean(low))

ggplot(bw_props, aes(x = weight, y = proportion)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkcyan") +
  geom_point(color = "indianred", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Mother's weight at last menstrual period (pounds)",
       y = "Proportion with low birth weight")
```

</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: fit the model, fill in the blanks</h3>

Now, let's fit a logistic regression model to predict low birth weight from mother's weight. Fill in the outcome (`low`) and predictor (`lwt`).

```{webr-r}
bw_model <- glm(____ ~ ____, family = binomial, data = birthwt)
summary(bw_model)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
bw_model <- glm(low ~ lwt, family = binomial, data = birthwt)
summary(bw_model)
```

In the coefficients table you should see (rounded):

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept)  0.9983     0.7853     1.27    0.204
lwt         -0.0141     0.0062    -2.28    0.023 *
```

</details>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: add the fitted logistic curve</h3>

Now use the fitted model to get predicted probabilities across a range of weights. Then draw the curve with `geom_line()`. The points are the observed proportions from the weight bands.

```{webr-r}
# Predicted probabilities from bw_model.
weight_line <- data.frame(lwt = seq(min(birthwt$lwt), max(birthwt$lwt), by = 1))
weight_line$prob <- predict(bw_model, newdata = weight_line, type = "response")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = weight_line, aes(x = lwt, y = prob), color = "gold") +
  geom_point(data = bw_props, aes(x = weight, y = proportion),
             color = "indianred", size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Mother's weight at last menstrual period (pounds)",
       y = "Probability of low birth weight")
```

</div>

<div class="svg-panel">
<svg viewBox="0 0 860 230" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Two S curves showing positive and negative coefficients">
  <g>
    <rect x="20" y="15" width="390" height="200" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d0dede"/>
    <text x="215" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#00565e">Positive coefficient (b1 &gt; 0)</text>
    <line x1="60" y1="185" x2="380" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <line x1="60" y1="185" x2="60" y2="60" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <text x="52" y="66" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" fill="#5d7475">1</text>
    <text x="52" y="189" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" fill="#5d7475">0</text>
    <text x="220" y="207" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" fill="#5d7475">predictor (e.g. age)</text>
    <path d="M 65 180 C 160 178, 180 70, 375 65" fill="none" stroke="#287a4d" stroke-width="3"/>
    <text x="115" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#287a4d" font-weight="700">probability goes UP</text>
  </g>
  <g>
    <rect x="450" y="15" width="390" height="200" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d0dede"/>
    <text x="645" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="700" fill="#00565e">Negative coefficient (b1 &lt; 0)</text>
    <line x1="490" y1="185" x2="810" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <line x1="490" y1="185" x2="490" y2="60" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.5"/>
    <text x="482" y="66" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" fill="#5d7475">1</text>
    <text x="482" y="189" text-anchor="end" font-size="12" fill="#5d7475">0</text>
    <text x="650" y="207" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" fill="#5d7475">predictor (e.g. mother's weight)</text>
    <path d="M 495 65 C 590 70, 610 178, 805 180" fill="none" stroke="#b83b3b" stroke-width="3"/>
    <text x="695" y="105" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#b83b3b" font-weight="700">probability goes DOWN</text>
  </g>
</svg>
<p class="svg-caption">The sign of the coefficient sets the direction of the curve. When the coefficient is positive, the probability rises as the predictor increases. When it is negative, the probability falls.</p>
</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: predict by hand, fill in the blanks</h3>

Let's predict the probability of a low birth weight baby for a mother who weighs 120 pounds. Fill in the intercept (`0.9983`) and the `lwt` coefficient (`-0.0141`).

```{webr-r}
# Probability of low birth weight when the mother weighs 120 pounds.
1 / (1 + exp(-(____ + ____ * 120)))
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
1 / (1 + exp(-(0.9983 + -0.0141 * 120)))
```

This returns about `0.333`, so roughly a 33% predicted chance of a low birth weight baby. Note that this time $b_1$ is negative, so the linear score shrinks as weight goes up.

</details>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: check with predict()</h3>

Fill in the model name (`bw_model`) and type (`"response"`).

```{webr-r}
new_mothers <- data.frame(lwt = c(100, 130, 160))
predict(____, newdata = new_mothers, type = ____)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the output</summary>

```
     1      2      3
0.3995 0.3038 0.2225
```

The probabilities fall as the mother's weight rises, exactly what the negative coefficient promised.

</details>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "SIGMOID";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 6;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
